note: Real engine output captured live (not synthesized): the stdout blocks are the verbatim marker-delimited regions the shipped Tcl emits, and the two report_check_types regions are the same session's violator reports behind setup_violation_count/hold_violation_count. The design is combinational-only (the available liberty has no flip-flops), so every row is an output-setup / output-hold check against virtual capture clocks -- two path groups per side (oclk1: y1,y2; oclk2: y3), which is what exercises the global worst-first resort across groups. Engine facts verified on this capture: -slack_max is inclusive (<=) at the boundary, so the emitter's strict $s < 0 filter is what keeps zero-slack ends out; -group_path_count caps per path group, so the Python side re-sorts globally and trims to the request cap; path ends expose no path_group_name property, so the emitter iterates sta::path_group_names and -path_group [list $name] (list-quoting is load-bearing: a bare multi-word name like {gated clock} splits, warns 'unknown path group', and silently disables the filter).
